target.title: fix(browser): reject loose click coordinate numbers when normalizing actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Browser action requests could accept loose coordinate numbers for `clickCoords`, such as hexadecimal or exponent-form strings, when users or tools submit direct coordinate clicks through the browser `/act` workflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clickCoords` now uses browser-owned decimal-only finite coordinate parsing before dispatch, matching the existing Browser schema and CLI contract that allow fractional CSS-pixel coordinates while rejecting non-decimal numeric syntax. This is an owner-local browser route normalization fix only; it does not add config, compatibility aliases, or provider behavior.

## User Impact

Browser action callers get consistent validation for coordinate clicks: decimal and fractional coordinates continue to work, while hexadecimal and exponent-form strings are rejected before a click is dispatched.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Browser `/act` route normalization preserves decimal and fractional `clickCoords` coordinates, rejects loose numeric strings, and does not dispatch malformed coordinate clicks.
- Current PR head: `31a4da266410c811419e3d2d2089f5da1c25d28c`; matching proof tree: `8fd4782486b7012d911a12cb47be458d0f7e2d19`.
- Real Browser `/act` setup proof: a temporary no-repo-change proof script launched a fresh headless Chrome profile with remote debugging, started the product Browser control routes through `registerBrowserRoutes` and `createBrowserRouteContext`, opened a local HTML page, and posted directly to the real `/act` HTTP route. The successful fractional request went through Playwright and incremented the page's click counter; the rejected hexadecimal and exponent requests returned before dispatch, leaving the counter unchanged.

```text
Browser /act real setup proof (head 31a4da266410c811419e3d2d2089f5da1c25d28c)
Chrome CDP: http://127.0.0.1:65204 (temporary headless Chrome profile)
Browser control: http://127.0.0.1:65206
Test page: http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof
Opened targetId: 31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B
fractional clickCoords status/body: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof"}
click state after fractional: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof","result":{"clicks":1,"last":{"x":42,"y":44,"target":"target"}}}
hex clickCoords status/body: 400 {"error":"clickCoords requires non-negative x and y","code":"ACT_INVALID_REQUEST"}
exponent clickCoords status/body: 400 {"error":"clickCoords requires non-negative x and y","code":"ACT_INVALID_REQUEST"}
click state after rejected inputs: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof","result":{"clicks":1}}
```

- Focused tests / checks:
  - GitHub `Real behavior proof` check passed on the current head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29160425226/job/86564456291.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.normalize.test.ts` passed with 10 tests passing.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts --testNamePattern "malformed coordinate clicks|navigation \+ common act commands"` passed with 2 tests passing and 21 skipped.
  - `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: normalization accepts decimal fractional strings such as `x: "10.5", y: ".25"`; the real `/act` route accepts fractional `x: "42.5"`; and `/act` returns `ACT_INVALID_REQUEST` with `clickCoords requires non-negative x and y` for negative, hexadecimal, and exponent-form coordinate inputs before malformed clicks are dispatched.
